Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections, logical flow from introduction through method, experiments, and discussion. Ideas are articulated with explicit hypotheses and tiered eviction details. However, repeated disclaimers about mock data create minor redundancy and reduce conciseness.

Novelty.justification: Introduces retrieval-provenance (passage boundaries, Contriever scores) to guide KV cache eviction, extending MMR diversity to cache retention. This is a distinct advance over uniform attention-based policies (H2O, StreamingLLM). Correlation analysis (ρ=0.612) and task-aware diversity gains provide original empirical contributions, though core eviction mechanics build incrementally on prior work.

Soundness.justification: Methods are conceptually sound but experimental results rely entirely on CPU mock data calibrated to correlation results (h-e1). All F1/EM gains (15.35% relative, 98.9% of FullKV) are simulated; real GPU validation is explicitly deferred. Code contains import errors (ncclCommResume), incomplete implementations, and failed hypotheses (h-m3). Statistical tests and visualizations are generated from synthetic distributions, violating reproducibility and reliability criteria.

Significance.justification: Addresses an important problem (memory-efficient long-context RAG) with practical motivation. However, unverified mock results and single-model/single-dataset scope limit impact. Expected real gains are only 10-12%, and cross-dataset/model validation is absent, reducing lasting field contribution.

strengths: Clear algorithmic description of tiered provenance eviction + MMR diversity
Empirical correlation finding (Contriever ρ=0.612) linking retrieval to attention
weaknesses: All quantitative results derived from mock/synthetic data rather than real GPU inference
Critical CUDA incompatibility prevents actual experiments; claims rest on unverified simulations
